blocks.text: This page tracks the Squamish MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $1,100,500 for a typical home, down 1.6% over twelve months.
Squamish benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Squamish home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,100,500 in October 2026. That is little changed at +0.8% on the month, up 1.6% over three months, up 2.1% over six months and down 1.6% over the year. Over three years it is up 3.2%, and over five years up 7.4%.
The weakest one-year move in Squamish was for a townhouse homes at −6.2%; the strongest was a detached home at +0.7%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,681,800) and an apartment ($599,600) is $1,082,200, and a townhouse ($968,600) sits $369,000 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Squamish is 3.0% above. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 1.6% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Squamish ranks 8 by all-home benchmark, with Tsawwassen above it at $1,103,800 and Ladner below it at $1,023,500.

Detached homes in Squamish: benchmark $1,681,800, up 4.2% in a month, up 2.7% in three months, little changed at −0.7% in six months, little changed at +0.7% in a year, up 9.7% in three years and up 7.6% in five. That is 5.3% below the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Squamish: benchmark $968,600, down 4.1% in a month, down 3.1% in three months, down 3.4% in six months, down 6.2% in a year, down 5.7% in three years and up 7.4% in five. That is 3.8% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Squamish: benchmark $599,600, little changed at +1.0% in a month, up 9.8% in three months, up 21.9% in six months, little changed at −0.1% in a year, down 5.8% in three years and little changed at +0.3% in five. That is 11.0% below the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Squamish home is worth about $17,900 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,118,400. By type, detached homes gained about $11,700, from $1,670,100 to $1,681,800, townhouses lost about $64,000, from $1,032,600 to $968,600, and apartments lost about $600, from $600,200 to $599,600 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,077,900 six months ago and near $1,066,400 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $22,600 above the six-month mark and about $34,100 above the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Squamish benchmark is about $31,900 above the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $8,800 below.
The $1,100,500 Squamish figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Squamish?
faq.a: In October 2026, a typical Squamish home was $1,100,500, with detached at $1,681,800.

faq.q: Are Squamish home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Squamish is down 1.6% over twelve months and up 1.6% over three months.
